hypothesis: A bare unresolved Call name that matches one global Clay declaration is sufficient evidence to design direct cross-module ownership from name coincidence.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Bare name coincidence is still insufficient because lexical/local binding and callable-namespace rules can change ownership; an explicit scope/module/import contract is required before execution authority is selected.

unusual_experiment.name: BARE_GLOBAL_SHADOW_INVERSION
unusual_experiment.scope: local synthetic discriminator only; no product bytes and no accepted-VPS claim
unusual_experiment.interpretation: Supports the counterhypothesis at mechanism level: global name coincidence cannot by itself mint ownership.
unusual_experiment.limitation: Current ClayCode callable namespace/shadowing semantics are not promoted here. The current analyzer/evaluator dispatch ordinary Call by analyzed callee kind, while local Let bindings populate the value environment. This experiment therefore exposes a contract question, not a proven production bug.

grf_collapse.preferred_reality: Explicit scope/module/import ownership must precede promotion of bare cross-module Call candidates.
grf_collapse.counterevidence_preserved: ClayCode may intentionally define function calls in a namespace separate from local value bindings; if owner-fixed semantics choose that rule, the synthetic shadow control is not a language bug.
